My name is Agnes, and this small plot near the house I use for beans mixed with maize and pumpkins — that way if one crop fails, something still feeds my children. I cannot afford to buy fertilizer bags for the beans because I save what little money I have for the maize plot, which is bigger; but I will spread the manure from our goats and chickens on this plot before the rains. I keep my own bean seeds from last harvest like my mother taught me, and I weed by hand with my daughters since hiring people is expensive. The rains will water the plot — we have no pump here in Lilongwe village.
